overview: This enum chooses the color set used for a character Cursed Energy gauge in battle UI.

None.simple: A blank gauge style that removes the normal gauge colors.
None.technical: Declared as the zero value of the uint8 enum. UGameBattleCharacterStatusWidget::UpdateCursedEnergyGaugeColor and UGameBattlePlayerInfoWidget::UpdateCursedEnergyGaugeColor pass this value to SetGaugeColor when the override flag is set. SetGaugeColor stores it and fetches its entry from CursedEnergyGaugeParameterMap, so the override uses whatever color block is registered for this key. No exported CharacterUI row uses the value.

JujutsuSorcerers.simple: The standard Cursed Energy gauge style used by most sorcerers.
JujutsuSorcerers.technical: Declared as uint8 slot 1. This is the fallback when a CharacterUI row is missing, used by the button guide root, the battle character data reader, and the VS-enemy interval character widget. The exported CharacterUIDataTable has 22 rows with this value. Those rows supply UI->CursedEnergyGaugeType, which the gauge, button guide, command list, and interval widgets pass to GetCursedEnergyGaugeParameter for a color block.

CursedSpirits.simple: The gauge style used for cursed spirits.
CursedSpirits.technical: Declared as uint8 slot 2. Twenty exported CharacterUIDataTable rows carry this value, including CP_130 through CP_160, CP_230, CP_250, CP_260, and the CN_ series. The row value reaches UGameBattleCursedEnergyGaugeWidget::SetGaugeColor and the other color consumers as a uint8 key into CursedEnergyGaugeParameterMap. The map has no entry in this checkout, so the exact colors for this key are unresolved.

Physical.simple: The gauge style for fighters whose resource is Physical Strength.
Physical.technical: Declared as uint8 slot 3. The exported CharacterUIDataTable uses it on CP_060 and CP_200, and both rows also set CharacterEnergyType to Physical. The gauge type is read as a color-map key by the battle HUD and command list. The resource labeling itself is driven by the separate CharacterEnergyType field, so this value selects colors only.

CP_020.simple: A special gauge style reserved for the character CP_020.
CP_020.technical: Declared as uint8 slot 4 and named after a character id. The export has exactly one CharacterUIDataTable row with this value, the row keyed CP_020, and CP_020 also appears in a command list energy-type check. The row value flows unchanged into GetCursedEnergyGaugeParameter, where it selects the color block registered under this key. The block itself is not present in the reconstructed source.

CP_110.simple: A special gauge style reserved for the character CP_110.
CP_110.technical: Declared as uint8 slot 5 and named after a character id. The export has exactly one CharacterUIDataTable row with this value, the row keyed CP_110. That row supplies UI->CursedEnergyGaugeType, which the battle HUD passes to GetCursedEnergyGaugeParameter as the map key for its color block. The block itself is not present in the reconstructed source.

Invalid.simple: A reserved unset marker used before gauge setup.
Invalid.technical: Declared as the uint8 slot 255 in the enum header. UGameBattleButtonGuideWidget initializes its GaugeType member to this value, and UGameBattleCursedEnergyGaugeWidget initializes both GaugeType and DefaultGaugeType to it before SetupGauge runs. No source branch compares against Invalid and no exported row carries it, so its behavior after a premature color request is unresolved.

notes: FGameDataTableRow_CharacterUI defaults CursedEnergyGaugeType to None, and the character UI export contains no None or Invalid row.

UGameWidgetCharacterParameter stores the color sets in CursedEnergyGaugeParameterMap, keyed by this enum. A missing key yields a value-initialized FGameWidgetCursedEnergyGaugeParameter. The map entries are not in the reconstructed source, so exact per-type colors are not asserted here.
The same type is passed to the battle gauge, the button guide colors, the command list gauges, the player status effects, and the VS-enemy interval gauge.

Fallbacks are caller-specific. The button guide root, battle character data reader, and VS-enemy interval widget use JujutsuSorcerers when the character UI row is missing, while the command list dereferences the row directly.
None has a traced color override path, while Invalid appears only as an uninitialized widget state.
